subject: Onramp bridge: procurement checklist for hybrid sourcing
messages:
From: Felipe Santos <felipe.santos@novacompute.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Sep 2027 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: OEM lead times + provisional ETA matrix for AcmeAI onramp

Karthik —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a provisional ETA matrix for the recommended SKUs (40GB and 80GB variants) across our factories and freight lanes. High-level notes: 

- 40GB (Q4 batch): earliest ship week is 2027-11-08, optimistic delivery to US West dock ~2027-11-22.
- 80GB (higher-priority tranche): earliest ship week 2027-12-06; typical customs + rack QC adds ~2–3 weeks.
- We can prioritize your order for a 2–4 week compression window for an additional 8% premium (limited to first 200 units).

Risks we flagged: PSU shortages may create spot delays; we recommend splitting the order across two production lanes to hedge. If Redwood needs staggered delivery, we can provide partial ship notices and a rolling invoice.

Attachment: OEM_ETA_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet; contains SKU by factory, lane, ship week, and prob. delay)

Would appreciate confirmation on:
1) Target mix between 40GB / 80GB for the initial tranche (we used 60/40 in the attached).
2) Whether Redwood wants the premium priority lane for a portion of the order.
3) Any required export paperwork that AcmeAI will provide (customer POs often speed customs).

Happy to jump on a quick sync with procurement and cloud ops later this week.

Best,
Felipe Santos
Director, Strategic Accounts — NovaCompute
felipe.santos@novacompute.com
+1 (415) 555-0219

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: felipe.santos@novacompute.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Sep 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM lead times + provisional ETA matrix for AcmeAI onramp

Felipe —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the ETA matrix. A couple immediate items from our side:

- AcmeAI (deal DL-2027-0912-A) expects a stepped onramp: 120 GPUs in month 1, add 360 over months 2–4. They are flexible on model family (we'll decide 40GB vs 80GB mix based on cost/latency tradeoffs).
- We need an explicit fallback plan: if OEM shipments slip beyond the optimistic window, can NovaCompute coordinate on expedited freight or split shipments across alternative ports?

Laura — can you share the recommended staging pool size and the non-blocking capacity we can hold on cloud (Stratus) for a 6–8 week bridge?

Ben — Acme's procurement team is asking for a committed delivery window and potential credit if Redwood can't hit the November/December onramp. We should surface the margin impact of buying priority lanes vs. standing capacity on Stratus.

Action ask: Felipe, please return a revised sheet with a column that includes: (a) guaranteed ship week (with contractual language), (b) expedited premium cost, and (c) alternate-lane ETA if we split across factories.

Thanks — available for a 30m sync Thursday afternoon.

— Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, felipe.santos@novacompute.com
Date: Wed, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM lead times + provisional ETA matrix for AcmeAI onramp

Team — quick context from the deal: AcmeAI is on a tight launch calendar and will escalate if the first tranche misses their November window. They asked for a firm SLA in the contract (delivery dates + remedies). They also signalled willingness to sign a 12-month Dedicated commitment if we can guarantee the initial onramp cadence.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- Buying the premium 8% lane for 200 units would cover the month-1 need and give us cushion; cost impact on the deal is material but could be amortized across the dedicated commit.
- Stratus cloud backfill: they offered a 6–10 week guaranteed capacity contract (pay-as-you-reserve) with a 30% premium vs on-demand. This is workable as a short-term bridge but doubles OpEx for those tokens.

Ask: Laura, can you run a margin sensitivity for these two options (premium OEM lane vs Stratus 6–10 week reserve) and include headroom for QC failures (we assume 2% DOA / rework)? Need by EOD Friday so I can include in the pricing appendix for Acme.

Ben
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: capacity@stratuscloud.com <capacity@stratuscloud.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Sep 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stratus provisional backfill terms for Redwood / AcmeAI

Hi Laura / Karthik —

Following up from our internal ops review. High level: Stratus can provide a reserved backfill pool for 6–10 weeks that guarantees N GPU slots with the following constraints:

- Lead time to reserve capacity and validate networking: ~7 calendar days post-PO.
- Commitment tiers: 6 weeks (flat fee), 8 weeks (5% discount), 10 weeks (10% discount).
- Onboarding includes a staging VPC and sample routing policy; we estimate a 48–72 hour readiness window after capacity is provisioned.
- Termination protections: Stratus will provide pro-rated credits if capacity is terminated >14 days before start of reserved window.

Attachment: Stratus_cap_backfill_terms.pdf (summary of terms + standard AUP)

We can also pre-wire a cross-connect and hold a soft reservation for Redwood for up to 4 business days while you finalize the PO.

Best,
Stratus Capacity Ops (capacity@stratuscloud.com)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 23:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Onramp bridge: procurement checklist for hybrid sourcing

Team — consolidation & next steps after the sync with Felipe / Stratus: 

1) Shortlist and decision windows
- Immediate (by EOD Monday): decide whether to buy premium lane for 160 units (covers month‑1 plus 40 units buffer) or rely on Stratus 6–8 week bridge. Ben to surface price delta in the deal appendix.

2) Contracting asks (Procurement)
- Felipe / NovaCompute: revise the ETA matrix with the three columns requested (guaranteed ship week, expedited premium cost, alt-lane ETA). We will attach that as a delivery schedule exhibit in the Redwood-Acme SOW.
- Marissa: draft the SOW language for delivery remedies (partial credits if initial tranche misses >7 days). Keep remedies capped to avoid financial overexposure.

3) Operational bridge
- Laura: provision a staging pool size = 80 GPUs (non-blocking on Stratus) to accept early traffic; this reduces risk for month‑1. Coordinate with Stratus ops to lock the 7-day soft reservation.

4) Logistics & export paperwork
- Vanessa: confirm which export docs Acme will provide and whether Redwood should file as importer of record for the 40GB tranche.

5) Customer communication
- Ben: align with Elaine (Acme procurement) on the hybrid plan and one-time premium ask. Share the timeline and the explicit tradeoffs so their execs can sign the Dedicated commit quickly if they want a lower unit price.

Files saved: Acme_signed_mop_notes.txt (customer mobility / export notes), OEM_ETA_matrix.xlsx, Stratus_cap_backfill_terms.pdf.

I'll collate the three vendor responses into a single delivery exhibit and share for legal review on Monday. Thanks all — good progress.

— Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
